policies.title: Privacy policy
policies.body:
Last updated: 14 September 2026

Who we are and how to contact us

Curtains UK is operated by Apex Curtains Ltd trading as Curtains UK. We are responsible for the personal information we use to provide the Curtains UK website, consultations and orders.

Apex Curtains Ltd trading as Curtains UK
36–44 Bolton Road
Blackburn
BB2 3FA
Email: enquiries@curtainsuk.com

Information we use

  • Contact and order information, including your name, email, delivery and billing details, products, selected fabrics, measurements, configuration, order history and payment status.
  • Messages and information you provide when asking for help, arranging a quote, or contacting us about an order or privacy request.
  • Optional consultation information, including your answers, design preferences, reference image, suggested and confirmed palettes, corrections, reactions, recommendations and sample or curtain journey events.
  • Technical information needed to operate and protect the website, including device and browser information, IP address, session identifiers, cookies and security or error logs.

Payment details are processed through the payment provider selected at checkout. Our curtain consultation does not need your card details. Please do not send payment details by email or include them in an uploaded image.

Why we use this information

We use information to respond to enquiries, provide consultations and quotes, calculate and fulfil your chosen curtain or sample order, process payments, arrange delivery, provide customer support and preserve your choices when you return.

We also use relevant records to protect the service, prevent fraud, investigate errors, assess recommendation quality and improve the customer experience. We use order and transaction records where needed to meet accounting and other legal obligations.

Our legal bases are taking steps at your request before a contract and performing that contract; compliance with legal obligations; and our legitimate interests in operating, securing and improving the service, subject to your rights. Where consent is required, including for non-essential cookies or separately permitted image-training use, we ask for it. You may withdraw consent without affecting the lawfulness of earlier processing.

Optional room and reference images

You may provide a maximum of one reference image per consultation. Uploading is optional: you can use the guided questions or browse fabrics without an image.

Your image is processed privately to help identify visible colours and design context for your consultation. It has no public image URL. You can keep, remove, add or move colours before confirming your palette. The original machine observation is kept separately from your confirmed palette.

Raw reference images are automatically deleted no later than 30 days after upload. The current service discards the raw image after analysis, so deletion currently happens sooner; it does not keep a raw-image archive. You may request earlier deletion by emailing enquiries@curtainsuk.com with your consultation reference. Please do not resend the image with your request.

Derived palette, recommendation and feedback records may be retained where required for service operation and improvement. These include your answers, original colour observation, confirmed palette, corrections, image hash, analysis version and journey events. An image hash is an identifier, not a viewable image.

We do not use customer-uploaded room or reference images for model training without separate explicit permission. Individual corrections and reactions do not automatically retrain or change our recommendation system. Please avoid including people, addresses, documents or other unnecessary personal information in images.

Who receives information

We use Shopify to operate the storefront and checkout, the payment providers available at checkout, and technical providers supporting hosting, data storage, private image analysis and communications. Relevant order and delivery information may be shared with those helping us make and deliver your order. These services receive information needed for their role. We may also disclose information where required by law or to protect legal rights.

Some service providers may process information outside the UK. The arrangements depend on the provider and service. You can contact us for information about the providers and transfer protections relevant to your information. Shopify explains its processing and international arrangements in its privacy policy.

Cookies and saved choices

The website uses cookies and browser storage for functions such as the basket, checkout, session security and remembering your consultation or selected fabric. Browser settings let you manage or remove stored information; doing so may clear saved choices or prevent parts of the service from working. Where non-essential cookies require consent, use the privacy choices presented on the website.

How long we keep information

The raw-image limit is set out above. Other information is retained only for as long as needed for its purpose. We consider whether a consultation or order is still active, whether you need to resume your choices, outstanding support or refund requests, service-quality and security investigations, and applicable accounting, legal and dispute requirements. Derived consultation records may be kept where needed to operate or improve the service; this does not extend raw-image retention or permit image training without separate permission.

Your choices and rights

Depending on the circumstances, you can ask to access, correct or erase your personal information, restrict or object to its use, or receive a portable copy. Contact enquiries@curtainsuk.com to make a request. We may need to verify your identity, and some information may need to be retained to meet legal obligations or resolve a claim.

HCI offers design suggestions. You can correct the palette, choose whether to follow a recommendation, or browse independently. Recommendations do not make decisions about your legal rights.

If you have a concern, please contact us using the details above. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Changes to this notice

We may update this notice to reflect changes to the service or our obligations. The date above identifies this version. If we propose a new use that requires your consent, we will ask separately.

policies.title: Refund policy
policies.body:
We have a 30-day return policy, which means you have 30 days after receiving your item to request a return.

To be eligible for a return, your item must be in the same condition that you received it, unworn or unused, with tags, and in its original packaging. You’ll also need the receipt or proof of purchase.

To start a return, you can contact us at enquiries@curtainsuk.com. If your return is accepted, we’ll send you a return shipping label, as well as instructions on how and where to send your package. Items sent back to us without first requesting a return will not be accepted.

You can always contact us for any return question at enquiries@curtainsuk.com


Damages and issues
Please inspect your order upon reception and contact us immediately if the item is defective, damaged or if you receive the wrong item, so that we can evaluate the issue and make it right.


Exceptions / non-returnable items
Certain types of items cannot be returned, like perishable goods (such as food, flowers, or plants), custom products (such as special orders or personalized items), and personal care goods (such as beauty products). We also do not accept returns for hazardous materials, flammable liquids, or gases. Please get in touch if you have questions or concerns about your specific item.

Unfortunately, we cannot accept returns on sale items or gift cards.


Exchanges
The fastest way to ensure you get what you want is to return the item you have, and once the return is accepted, make a separate purchase for the new item.


Refunds
We will notify you once we’ve received and inspected your return, and let you know if the refund was approved or not. If approved, you’ll be automatically refunded on your original payment method. Please remember it can take some time for your bank or credit card company to process and post the refund too.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.body:
• What is the acoustic panel made of?

The panel is made of a black acoustic felt (made of recycelt plastic). On top of that you find the slats with an MDF core and a veneer surface.

 

  • How do I clean the acoustic panels?

You best use a duster or a vacuum cleaner for the cleaning.

 

  • Is the felt breathable?

Yes, our acoustic felt is breathable.

 

  • Are the surfaces treated? Can I oil them?

The surfaces are in principle untreated.
They can be oiled with a wood oil (not cooking oil) and a sponge or towel.

 

  • What about the UV stability of the surfaces?

The wood surfaces are untreated and will therefore change over time due to the effects of light. The light, classical oak, for example, turns typically a little yellowish.

 

  • Do the panels also insulate the sound to the outside?

Unfortunately, the panels won’t stop sound from wandering from room to room (or floor to floor) – their main purpose is to absorb reverberation and prevent it from being reflected back into the room.

If you want to stop sound coming from a neighbour or a room, it needs good cavity insulation between walls or floors – and maybe more.

 

  • On what surfaces can I install the panel?

The installation is possible on nearly every surface, even on brick walls and concrete.

 

  • Can I use the panels in the bathroom?

In general, we do not recommend its use in damp rooms. The core consists of an MDF board, which could maybe swell.

Nevertheless, some of our customers have used the acoustic panels in the bathroom and are very satisfied.

However, it should be made sure that the product does not come into direct contact with water.

 

  • How do I install electric lights and sockets?

You can cut a hole into the panels and  extract the socket end of the panel wall.

Use electrician. 

 

  • How shall I mount the panels?

If the panels are mainly used for visual purposes, it is possible to attach them directly to the wall. For this, we recommend the use of (black) screws, which are then drilled directly through the felt into the wall or also glued to the wall with mounting glue.

To achieve sound class A, we recommend the mounting on 45mm thick battens. The resulting gap is then lined with mineral wool (we recommend Isover or Rockwool).

 

  • Do you provide an installation service?

We will come and install the panels , so you can sit back and relax.

 

  • Can I place pictures on the panels?

The picture frames can be stuck on with Tesa Foto Stripes, for example.
Alternatively, a small nail/screw can be drilled through the felt into the wall.

 

  • Can I hide cables behind the panels?

This depends on the thickness of the cables.


In general, the cables are simply positioned behind the panel, because the felt is very flexible and gives space at this point.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.body:
Measuring & Ordering

Q: How do I measure for curtains?
A: Measure the full width of your window or pole including 10–15 cm overlap on each side. For drop, measure from the rod or track to 1 cm above the floor (or sill). See our detailed guide: How to Measure Curtains.

Q: What fullness should I choose?
A:

  • Sheers & lightweight fabrics: 1.5× fabric width

  • Standard drapes: 2× fabric width

  • Luxury pinch/goblet pleats: 2.5–3× fabric width

Heading Styles & Hardware

Q: Which heading style works best with tracks?
A: Wave (ripple fold) and pencil pleat headings glide smoothly on tracks. For rods, consider eyelet, tab‑top, or pinch pleat. Explore styles: Curtain Heading Styles.

Q: Can I use my existing poles or tracks?
A: In most cases, yes. Provide us with your current rod/track length and type during your consultation, and we’ll advise on compatibility or recommend hardware upgrades. Check our hardware range: Curtain Hardware & Tracks.

Fabrics & Linings

Q: Do I need blackout lining?
A: Choose blackout lining for bedrooms, nurseries, or media rooms to block up to 99% of light and improve insulation. Standard lining offers UV protection and added weight. Learn more: Curtain Linings.

Q: What fabrics are best for thermal efficiency?
A:

  • Thermal fleece linings or interlining behind heavy fabrics (velvet, chenille) trap heat.

  • Thicker cotton or acrylic blends offer natural insulation for daytime use.

Installation & Service

Q: Do you offer professional installation?
A: Yes—our certified fitters handle everything from accurate measuring to flawless hanging, including all hardware. Book now: Installation Service.

Q: What’s the turnaround time?
A: Custom curtains typically dispatch in 2–3 weeks. Installation appointments can be scheduled immediately upon delivery.

Care & Maintenance

Q: How do I wash my curtains?
A:

  • Machine‑washable fabrics: Gentle cycle, cold water, air‑dry.

  • Heavier or interlined curtains: Dry clean only.

  • Always check care labels and remove hooks or rings before cleaning.

Q: How can I remove wrinkles?
A: Use a handheld steamer on low heat. For wave or pencil pleats, steam from the back to maintain fold shape.

Safety & Compliance

Q: Are your curtains child‑safe?
A: We offer cordless and tension‑rod systems to eliminate dangling cords, meeting the latest safety regulations for children’s rooms. .

Q: Do you provide fire‑retardant fabrics?
A: Yes—select fire‑retardant polyester options, ideal for commercial settings or nurseries. Contact us for certification details.

Still Have Questions?

If you don’t see your question here, get in touch with our design team or call us at 0800 772 067. We’re happy to help!

pages.title: Fabric Care Guide
pages.body:
Choose the Right Fabric — Keep It Looking Beautiful

Curtains don’t just add style — the fabric you choose affects how your room feels, how much light it blocks, and how long it lasts. This guide helps you understand the most popular curtain fabrics and how to care for them properly.

🧵 Popular Curtain Fabrics

1. Cotton

  • Look & Feel: Natural, breathable, and versatile.

  • Best For: Living rooms, bedrooms.

  • Care: Machine washable (check label), low-heat iron.

2. Linen / Linen Look

  • Look & Feel: Light, airy, slightly textured.

  • Best For: Light-filled rooms and relaxed settings.

  • Care: Dry clean or gentle wash; may wrinkle.

3. Velvet

  • Look & Feel: Luxurious, thick, and elegant.

  • Best For: Bedrooms, formal lounges, thermal insulation.

  • Care: Dry clean only; use a soft brush for dusting.

4. Polyester / Blends

  • Look & Feel: Durable, crease-resistant, low-maintenance.

  • Best For: Busy households, children's rooms.

  • Care: Machine washable, easy iron.

5. Silk / Faux Silk

  • Look & Feel: Smooth, elegant, and light-reflective.

  • Best For: Formal settings and statement windows.

  • Care: Dry clean only; avoid direct sunlight to prevent fading.

6. Blackout Lining

  • Purpose: Blocks out light, adds insulation.

  • Best For: Bedrooms, nurseries, home theatres.

  • Care: Spot clean or dry clean depending on outer fabric.

🧼 General Curtain Care Tips

  • Dust regularly using a vacuum with a soft brush attachment.

  • Steam to remove creases (avoid direct contact for delicate fabrics).

  • Always follow care label instructions.

  • Avoid machine washing lined or heavy curtains unless label says otherwise.

  • For dry clean only fabrics, take to a professional to preserve the quality.

✂️ Made-to-Measure Notes

All made-to-measure curtains from CurtainsUK.com are hand-finished with care. We recommend checking care instructions before cleaning to protect your investment.

pages.title: Curtain Fabric Colour Guide
pages.body:
Choosing the right curtain colour can completely transform your space. Whether you're looking to create a calm retreat, a vibrant statement, or a timeless backdrop, our colour guide will help you pick the perfect shade for your home.

1. Consider the Room's Purpose

  • Living Room: Neutrals like beige, grey, and soft white create a welcoming atmosphere. For a bold look, try navy, forest green, or deep burgundy.

  • Bedroom: Opt for calming colours such as dusty pink, lavender, or cool blues to promote relaxation.

  • Kitchen/Dining: Light colours like cream, pale yellow, or light grey keep things airy and fresh.

Learn more about Curtain measuring 

2. Match or Contrast With Walls

  • Matching tones blend seamlessly and make the space feel larger and more cohesive.

  • Contrasting colours can create visual interest. For example, grey walls pair beautifully with mustard, teal, or blush curtains.

3. Natural Light & Fabric Weight

  • In bright rooms, darker colours won’t overpower the space and can add depth.

  • In low-light rooms, lighter colours help reflect light and make the space feel bigger.

  • Heavier fabrics in darker colours are ideal for blocking light and adding warmth.

4. Timeless vs. Trendy

  • Timeless shades like white, grey, taupe, and navy offer flexibility and longevity.

  • Trendy colours such as sage green, terracotta, and blush pink bring a modern flair—but consider how often you like to redecorate.

5. Mood & Style Influence

  • Warm colours (red, orange, yellow) energise and uplift.

  • Cool colours (blue, green, purple) calm and soothe.

  • Earth tones feel grounded and natural—perfect for rustic or minimalist themes.

View Gallery 

6. Samples Help!

Always see the  fabric swatches to see how colours look in your actual space—lighting can dramatically change a shade throughout the day.
